This integration connects Gladys to your **Foscam IP cameras**, directly on
your local network: camera images, motion / person / sound alarms, motion
detection on or off, night vision, and for motorized models, pan / tilt and
saved positions.

It talks to each camera through its built-in HTTP API (the Foscam "CGI"). No
Foscam cloud, no Foscam account, no internet connection is involved: the
transport badge of every camera reads **local**.

## Compatible cameras

The Foscam **HD** cameras, which all share the same API: FI98xx and FI99xx,
R2 / R4 / R5, C1 / C2 / C5, G2 / G4, SD2 / SD4, X1 / X2 / X5 and most of the
current indoor and outdoor models.

Not supported:

- the old MJPEG models (FI8xxx, port 80): their API is a different one;
- the models that only work through the Foscam app and cloud (some battery
  cameras): they do not answer on the local network.

When in doubt, the **Test the connection** button tells you within seconds
whether a camera answers.

## Before you start

1. **Give each camera a fixed IP address**, in your router (DHCP
   reservation) or in the camera (_Settings → Network → IP configuration_).
   The integration keys every camera on its MAC address, so a new address
   does not lose the camera, but it must be typed again in the
   configuration.
2. **Note the HTTP port** of the camera: _Settings → Network → Port_, the
   **HTTP port**. It is **88** out of the box.
3. **Create a dedicated user** on each camera (_Settings → System → Account
   management_), with the same name and password on every camera if you can:
   - role **administrator** if you want to arm or disarm the motion
     detection and change the night vision from Gladys;
   - role **operator** otherwise (images, alarms, PTZ).
4. **Set up the detection in the camera**: _Settings → Alarm → Motion
   detection_ (and _Sound detection_, _Human detection_ on the models that
   have it). The camera decides what is a detection — zones, sensitivity,
   schedule; the integration reads its alarms.

## Configuration

| Field                 | What to put in it                                                                              |
| --------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| **Cameras**           | The address of every camera, see below                                                         |
| **Username**          | The camera user (`admin` by default)                                                           |
| **Password**          | Its password                                                                                   |
| **Image refresh (s)** | Seconds between two images sent to Gladys, 60 by default, 5 minimum. `0` sends none on its own |
| **Alarm check (s)**   | Seconds between two reads of the camera alarms, 2 by default                                   |
| **PTZ step (ms)**     | How long a pan or tilt lasts before the integration stops it, 800 by default, 5000 at most     |

### The camera list

Type the IP addresses, separated by commas (or semicolons, or one per line):

```
192.168.1.20, 192.168.1.21
```

Add `:port` when the HTTP port is not 88, and `Name=` in front to choose the
name of the camera in Gladys (otherwise the name stored in the camera is
used):

```
Entrance=192.168.1.20, Garden=192.168.1.21:8080
```

A camera that needs **its own username or password**, or whose capabilities
must be forced, goes in a JSON list instead (the whole field is then that
list):

```json
[
  { "host": "192.168.1.20", "name": "Entrance" },
  { "host": "192.168.1.22", "port": 88, "name": "Garage", "username": "gladys", "password": "…" },
  { "host": "192.168.1.23", "name": "Living room", "ptz": true, "zoom": true }
]
```

| Key        | Meaning                                                                                   |
| ---------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `host`     | IP address or host name (required)                                                        |
| `port`     | HTTP port, 88 by default                                                                  |
| `name`     | Name in Gladys                                                                            |
| `username` | User of this camera, instead of the one of the configuration                              |
| `password` | Its password. Prefer the **Password** field: this one is not hidden in the form           |
| `ptz`      | `true` / `false` to force the pan and tilt controls (detected otherwise)                  |
| `zoom`     | `true` for the rare models with a motorized zoom: adds Zoom in / Zoom out to the controls |

An entry that cannot be read (a typo in the address, a port out of range,
the same camera twice) is ignored, and **Test the connection** says which one
and why.

## In Gladys

A camera shows up in **Discovery** as soon as it has answered once. Its
features (you can rename them in Gladys):

| Feature                      | What it does                                                                                                  |
| ---------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| **Image**                    | The camera image, refreshed every _Image refresh_ seconds and whenever Gladys asks for one                    |
| **Enabled in Gladys**        | Off: Gladys stops showing the camera, and the integration stops sending its images and detections             |
| **Motion**                   | 1 while the camera reports motion (or a person), 0 otherwise                                                  |
| **Motion detection**         | The motion detection of the camera, armed (1) or not (0). It can be switched from Gladys                      |
| **Night vision**             | The infrared LEDs, on or off. Switching it from Gladys forces them; `set_night_vision` puts them back on auto |
| **Move** (motorized cameras) | Pan left / right, tilt up / down (and zoom, when declared)                                                    |
| **Preset** (motorized)       | The positions saved in the camera, by name                                                                    |

**Enabled in Gladys** is a Gladys-side privacy switch: the camera itself
keeps running, recording to its SD card and sending its own notifications.

### Images

Gladys takes images of 150 KB at most. A Foscam snapshot is a frame of the
main stream (often 200 to 400 KB in 1080p): the integration scales it down
before sending it, keeping the ratio.

Every detection also sends a fresh image right away, so that a scene sending
the camera image on a detection sends the frame of that detection.

### Motorized cameras

The Foscam API has no "one step" movement: a move runs until it is stopped.
The integration therefore stops **every move** after _PTZ step_
milliseconds (5 s at most), so that a lost stop never leaves the camera
grinding against its end stop. Lengthen the step for a bigger movement.

The presets are read when the camera is discovered. After adding or
renaming one in the camera, run a new scan in **Discovery**: the list is
updated without re-creating the camera.

## Test the connection

The **Test the connection** button of the Configuration screen asks every
camera, right now, who it is. For each camera you get the model, the
firmware and whether it is motorized — or the exact reason why it does not
answer:

| Message                         | What to do                                                                                    |
| ------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| nothing answers at this address | Check the IP address and the HTTP port; the camera must be on the same network as Gladys      |
| no answer in time               | The camera is off, rebooting, or its Wi-Fi is too weak                                        |
| wrong username or password      | Check them on the camera. After a few failures the camera locks the account for a few minutes |
| this account is not allowed     | Give the user the administrator or operator role                                              |
| not a Foscam camera API         | Something else answers on that port: check the HTTP port                                      |

After a wrong password, the integration stops asking that camera for five
minutes: insisting would get the account locked.

## Scenes and dashboard (Gladys 5.1+)

### Scene triggers

- **Camera detection** (`detection`): a camera raised an alarm. Filter on
  the camera and on what was detected: `motion`, `person`, `sound`, `io`
  (the alarm input of the camera). The scene reads
  `{{triggerEvent.data.kind}}` and `{{triggerEvent.data.camera_name}}`. One
  event per alarm, never one per read.
- **Camera offline or back** (`camera_connection`): a camera stopped
  answering (three reads in a row, or a wrong password), or answers again.
  The scene reads `{{triggerEvent.data.state}}` (`offline` / `online`),
  `{{triggerEvent.data.camera_name}}` and `{{triggerEvent.data.reason}}`.

The **Motion** feature also drives the standard "device state" trigger of
Gladys.

### Scene actions

Each action answers an output the next actions can test; a camera that
cannot carry it out answers `false` instead of stopping the scene.

| Action                                                      | Fields                       | Output     |
| ----------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------- | ---------- |
| **Take a camera snapshot** (`take_snapshot`)                | camera                       | `captured` |
| **Move camera to a preset** (`goto_preset`)                 | camera, preset name          | `moved`    |
| **Arm or disarm motion detection** (`set_motion_detection`) | camera, armed                | `applied`  |
| **Set night vision** (`set_night_vision`)                   | camera, automatic / on / off | `applied`  |
| **Reboot a camera** (`reboot_camera`)                       | camera                       | `rebooted` |

`take_snapshot` followed by the Gladys action **Send camera image** sends a
picture taken at that very moment. Typical scenes: arm the motion detection
of every camera when the house is empty, send the camera to its door preset
when the doorbell rings.

### Widgets

- **Foscam camera**: one camera, chosen in the widget settings: its last
  image, the live motion tile, connection, motion detection, night vision,
  last detection, and buttons to refresh the image and to arm or disarm the
  detection.
- **Foscam cameras**: every camera at a glance (online, offline, in alarm),
  with a button that refreshes every image.

## Security

- The Foscam API takes the username and password in the address of every
  request, over plain HTTP: they cross your local network in clear. Use a
  **dedicated user**, not the camera's main account, and keep the cameras on
  a network you trust.
- **Do not expose the cameras to the internet** (port forwarding, UPnP): the
  integration does not need it. Turn UPnP and P2P off in the camera if you do
  not use the Foscam app.
- Keep the camera firmware up to date.
- The password is stored by Gladys in a secret field; the integration never
  writes it to its logs nor to its own files.

## Troubleshooting

- **The camera does not show up in Discovery**: it has never answered. Run
  **Test the connection**.
- **Motion stays at 0**: the motion detection must be armed and configured in
  the camera (zones, schedule). The **Motion detection** feature tells
  whether it is armed.
- **"Motion detection" cannot be switched**: the user needs the
  administrator role.
- **The image is late**: lower **Image refresh**; Gladys takes 12 images a
  minute per camera at most, so 5 s is the floor.
- **Detailed logs**: they are in the integration logs (Gladys, Integrations,
  Foscam, logs).

## Configuration settings

These are the settings Foscam asks for in its configuration screen in Gladys.

| Setting | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Getting started | `section` | No | The integration talks to your Foscam cameras directly on your local network, through their HTTP API (CGI): no Foscam cloud, no account, no internet. Give each camera a fixed IP address in your router, then type those addresses below. Create a dedicated user on each camera (operator role) rather than using the admin account. |
| Cameras | `string` | Yes | IP addresses of your cameras, separated by commas. Add :port when it is not 88, and Name= in front to name a camera, e.g. Entrance=192.168.1.20, Garden=192.168.1.21:8080. A JSON array is accepted too, for a camera with its own credentials (see the documentation). |
| Username | `string` | Yes | User of the cameras (the same on every camera, unless set per camera in a JSON list). |
| Password | `secret` | No | Password of that user. Careful: after a few wrong passwords, a Foscam camera locks the account for a while. |
| Image refresh (s) | `number` | No | Seconds between two images sent to Gladys (5 minimum). 0 sends none: Gladys then asks for an image only when you open the camera. |
| Alarm check (s) | `number` | No | Seconds between two reads of the camera alarms (motion, person, sound). 2 catches every alarm. |
| PTZ step (ms) | `number` | No | Motorized cameras: how long a move lasts before the integration stops it, in milliseconds (5000 at most). |

## How to install Foscam in Gladys

1. In Gladys, open **Integrations**: Foscam appears in the catalog, next to the native integrations, with a community badge.
2. Click **Install**. Gladys pulls the Docker image (`ghcr.io/prohand/gladys-foscam:0.0.2`), starts it in a sandbox isolated from the core, and generates the integration's interface (devices, discovery and configuration).
3. Open the **Configuration** screen of the integration, fill in the settings, and save.
4. You can also install it directly from its repository URL: [https://github.com/prohand/gladys-foscam](https://github.com/prohand/gladys-foscam).

Foscam requires Gladys `>=5.1.0`. The catalog inside Gladys refreshes every hour, so a new version becomes available at most one hour after its release.

Not running Gladys yet? It is free and open source: [follow the installation guide](/docs/) to get started.

## About external integrations

Foscam is an **external integration**: a community integration packaged as a Docker container and published on GitHub, that Gladys installs in one click and runs in a sandbox isolated from its core. It is published and maintained by [prohand](https://github.com/prohand), not by the Gladys core team.
